facility_roles.note: Proposed surface detector at CERN; the official site does not name a specific interaction point (e.g. Point 5/CMS).

intervals.label: proposed
intervals.note: 2026-09-17 fixed-target verification: anchored on the MATHUSLA Letter of Intent, arXiv:1811.00927 ('A Letter of Intent for MATHUSLA: a dedicated displaced vertex detector above ATLAS or CMS', submitted 2 Nov 2018), which is the collaboration's first public proposal document. Previously `start: null`, which made the interval cover no year at all (A3: 'start: null covers only [lo(end), hi(end))'), so the derived state at the build date was `unrecorded` (None) rather than `proposed`, and `status` was written as `null` to match -- masking that MATHUSLA has, in fact, been an actively proposed experiment since 2018.
intervals.quote: we propose the construction of MATHUSLA

intervals.label: planned start (with HL-LHC)
intervals.quote: go online with the HL-LHC upgrade to the Large Hadron Collider in ~2029

quantity.display: 11 m tall (proposed 40 m x 40 m x 11 m decay volume)
quantity.note: Value/unit record only the height (11 m) of the proposed decay volume; the full footprint is carried in `display`. The collaboration is also reported to be revising this geometry to a smaller, cheaper design.

name: MATHUSLA
notes: Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

No new site created, per the brief: the official page states only that the surface location shields it from ATLAS/CMS backgrounds, without naming a specific interaction point (e.g. Point 5); no detector placement/site_id is recorded rather than guessing which LHC point.

accelerator_ids references accelerator:lhc (owned by the cern-atlas workstream) since MATHUSLA is explicitly tied to HL-LHC collisions as its particle source, not the SPS fixed-target programme; kept in this file despite being outside the classic 'fixed-target' sense because MATHUSLA is assigned to this workstream by the ID_REGISTRY.
No collaboration membership counts found on the official site.

2026-09-17 fixed-target verification: `status` was `null` because the sole 'proposed' interval had `start: null`, so no interval covered the build date and A3's derived state was `unrecorded`. A dated Letter of Intent (arXiv:1811.00927, 2 Nov 2018) anchors the interval's start, so the derived state -- and `status` -- is now `proposed`, honestly reflecting that MATHUSLA has been a standing proposal since 2018, not an unknown/unrecorded entity.

physics_goals.value: Detect neutral, weakly coupled, long-lived particles (LLPs) with masses above roughly 1 GeV and lifetimes up to the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis limit, produced in LHC proton-proton collisions

summary.plain: MATHUSLA is a proposed detector that would sit on the surface at CERN, far above the LHC's underground collisions, to catch new particles so weakly interacting and long-lived that they could fly through ordinary detectors unnoticed.
summary.technical: Proposed large-volume (40 m x 40 m x 11 m, under revision) surface detector near the LHC, designed to reconstruct displaced decay vertices of neutral long-lived particles produced in pp collisions, with a background-free environment enabled by its surface location and distance from the interaction point; proposed to come online with the HL-LHC upgrade (~2029).

unique_capabilities.quote: background free environment and no trigger limitations
unique_capabilities.value: A large (proposed 40 m x 40 m x 11 m) surface detector, shielded from beam-related backgrounds by its distance and position above ground, giving a background-free environment with no trigger limitations for reconstructing displaced LLP decay vertices; can also function as a cosmic-ray telescope
